daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The vacancy in the vice presidency following Gibran's resignation has triggered widespread speculation about his replacement, with several parties publicly backing DPR Speaker Sufmi Dasco Ahmad for the role. PAN endorsed Dasco as an "inclusive and problem solver" figure, while Gerindra's Maluku Utara chapter backed him for his ability to embrace all circles. Dasco himself responded to the mounting support by urging respect for the president's prerogative to choose. The MPR has prepared 22 requirements for vice presidential candidates and scheduled a plenary session for 9 December 2026, while the MPR received a letter from Prabowo regarding Gibran's replacement.

  • PDIP's Komarudin responded to Gibran's volunteer organization, stating he does not believe in "one family" politics.
  • A police ethics hearing for Irjen Eko Hadi over the presidential wiretapping case was held today, led by Komjen Hendro Pandowo.
  • DPR leadership stated that the right to express opinion regarding Gibran's diploma has automatically concluded.
  • Dasco announced the DPR will absorb public and legal expert input on the wiretapping bill.
  • A public petition demanding disclosure of all DPR members' diplomas has surpassed 21,000 signatures.
  • The MPR's assessment body discussed reconstruction of decentralization and local democracy.
  • Fadli Zon praised the DPD RI Awards for introducing local figures who had not received attention.
  • A Gerindra legislator called for the wiretapping bill to strictly limit law enforcement authority.

Foreign Policy & Defence

President Prabowo participated in several ASEAN summit meetings in the Philippines, pushing for stronger regional cooperation across multiple sectors. He encouraged stronger ASEAN-South Korea energy and maritime cooperation, while also highlighting future industries in ASEAN-Australia relations. Indonesia championed the RCEP agreement at the ASEAN-Korea Summit and announced it will seek expanded export access at the upcoming APEC Summit.

  • Indonesia urged strengthening of ASEAN crisis management mechanisms during the regional summits.
  • Indonesia called for tighter ASEAN coordination against transnational crime.
  • Indonesia urged international action against wildlife trafficking at the regional forum.
  • Indonesia urged ASEAN and Australia to expand study and work opportunities for regional youth.
  • Indonesia pushed for UN reform to strengthen world peace and stability.
  • Indonesia's ambassador to Uzbekistan received an award related to tolerance from the Uzbek government.
  • The Indonesian consulate in San Francisco introduced tempe and explored the food market at a festival.

Other

Bank Indonesia is projected to raise interest rates to 6 percent due to rupiah pressure, according to economic analysts. BI is projected to increase the benchmark rate as the rupiah remains under sustained pressure from global economic headwinds. The move would mark the central bank's latest effort to stabilize the currency and manage inflationary pressures heading into the end of the year.

  • Police are investigating alleged fraud by "Tenun Tonic" investment scheme that caused Rp 200 billion in losses to victims.
  • The national disaster agency proposed weather modification to minimize flood risks in Sumatra.
  • PERURI unveiled an e-passport chip prototype developed in collaboration with ITB.
  • OJK projects positive banking industry performance through 2027.
  • Bapanas stated farmers are free to sell corn above the government purchase price, with Bulog serving as a safety net.
